handbookNote: Massachusetts Real Estate Broker license exam. Genuinely NEW track -- Massachusetts previously had no broker-tier track on this site, only ma_re_salesperson. Exam vendor: PSI Services LLC, under contract with the Massachusetts Division of Occupational Licensure Board of Registration of Real Estate Brokers and Salespersons. PRIMARY-CONFIRMED by directly downloading and reading PSI's own official Massachusetts Real Estate Examination Candidate Information Bulletin (updated 09/23/2025) -- the mass.gov-hosted copy of this same bulletin returned HTTP 403 to both WebFetch and curl (mass.gov actively blocks non-browser requests at the edge, confirmed by testing multiple mass.gov URLs and a base64-blob extraction workaround that was itself blocked by a tool-level safety filter against returning base64 data), so the working copy was found and downloaded instead from PSI's own test-taker site (test-takers.psiexams.com/mare -> a direct Broker-specific bulletin link, bulletin id 4459, distinct from the Salesperson bulletin id 4460 -- a rare case where PSI publishes fully separate CIB documents per license tier rather than one shared document). Exam Summary Table, quoted directly from the bulletin: Broker exam General portion = 75 items (80 points possible -- a footnote states 'General broker exams include questions that are scored up to two points', disclosed here rather than silently flattened), 150 minutes; State portion = 40 items (40 points), 90 minutes; combined 240-minute time limit. Passing: the bulletin states a flat '70%' passing standard, and separately confirms candidates who pass one portion and fail the other need only retake the failed portion -- meaning each portion is independently scored and independently must clear 70%. NOTE ON A REAL SOURCE-DOCUMENT INCONSISTENCY: the bulletin's own summary table lists the Broker 'Both' row as '120 (120 points) 240 Minutes', but 75 general + 40 state = 115, not 120 -- this appears to be a copy-paste artifact from the Salesperson row directly above it (Salesperson General 80 + State 40 = 120, matching exactly), since the Broker General row's own 75-item figure and the 240-minute combined time are both internally consistent and separately corroborated. This build uses the more granular, self-consistent 115-item total (75+40) rather than the summary table's likely-erroneous 120, a resolution independently cross-checked against nj_re_broker.json's real, cleanly-confirmed 115-item/240-min/70%-pass/min_correct-81 structure -- New Jersey's Broker exam turns out to share an essentially identical mechanics profile with Massachusetts. track_registry models this as exam_question_count=115, exam_duration_sec=14400 (240 min), pass_percent=70, min_correct=81 (matching NJ's own resolved figure exactly, since 115 x 0.70 = 80.5, rounded to 81). 5-10 unscored experimental items may also appear. CONTENT OUTLINE -- General/national portion percentages, quoted verbatim from the bulletin (Broker column, summing to exactly 100% of the 75-item general portion, independently re-verified by hand this session): Property Ownership 10%, Land Use Controls 5%, Valuation 8%, Financing 9%, Contracts 19% (the largest single general topic), Agency 13%, Property Disclosures 7%, Property Management 5% (Broker-only sub-items), Transfer of Title 6%, Practice of Real Estate 12% (Broker-only supervisory sub-items), Real Estate Calculations 6%. NOTABLE: these percentages are IDENTICAL to New Jersey's, Tennessee's, and Virginia's own PSI-published general-portion percentages for the Broker exam (see nj_re_broker.json, tn_re_broker.json, va_re_broker.json) -- further confirms PSI uses one shared multi-state 'General Portion' content-outline template for real estate broker exams nationwide, with only the State-specific portion varying meaningfully by state. Massachusetts State portion, quoted verbatim as percentages and item counts (of the 40-item state portion, Broker column, summing to the full 40): Duties and Powers of the Board 5% (2 items), Licensing Requirements 10% (4 items), Requirements Governing Licensees 33-35% (14 items -- the largest single state topic), Contracts 5% (2 items), Consumer Protection Laws 10-12% (4 items), Environmental Issues and Hazardous Materials 10% (4 items), Massachusetts Fair Housing Law 10% (4 items), Landlord Tenant Law 10% (4 items), Additional Topics 5% (2 items). This bank's bucket sizing is directly proportional to these real, PSI-published weights, not an even split -- actual per-bucket counts were then set by each drafting pass to whatever its real, verifiable source material actually supported. Real Massachusetts statute/regulation facts independently verified this session via malegislature.gov (Massachusetts' official General Laws site -- mass.gov itself and 254 CMR pages returned 403s throughout this build, same as the bulletin download) -- M.G.L. Chapter 112, Sections 87PP through 87DDD½ (the Real Estate Brokers and Salespersons licensing statute) confirmed by direct fetch, notably: Sec. 87PP (broker/salesperson definitions), Sec. 87QQ/87RR (Board authority, valid-license requirement for commission actions), Sec. 87UU (corporate/individual license distinction), Sec. 87XX/87XX½ (disciplinary sanctions, continuing education), Sec. 87AAA/87AAA¾ (agency relationship disclosure, dual/designated agency, 1-4 unit scope), Sec. 87BBB (discriminatory-solicitation fines), Sec. 87YY½ (home inspection brochure and no-specific-recommendation rule, with a buyer's-broker exception); M.G.L. Chapter 186, Sec. 15B (the real, detailed Massachusetts security deposit statute -- 5% interest requirement, separate in-state bank account, 30-day bank-receipt requirement, 10-day statement-of-condition requirement, treble-damages penalty for violations); M.G.L. Chapter 93A, Secs. 2 and 9 (the Massachusetts Consumer Protection Act -- unfair/deceptive acts, 30-day demand letter requirement, double/treble damages, attorney's fees); M.G.L. Chapter 151B, Secs. 4 and 5 (Massachusetts Fair Housing Law -- protected classes beyond federal law including sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, ancestry, veteran/military status, source of income; MCAD enforcement, 300-day filing deadline, civil penalties up to $50,000); M.G.L. Chapter 111, Sec. 197 (the Massachusetts Lead Law -- child-under-6 trigger, 90-day new-owner compliance window); M.G.L. Chapter 148, Secs. 26F and 26F½ ('Nicole's Law' -- smoke detector and carbon monoxide alarm compliance at time of sale, the latter section number confirmed via the chapter's table of contents after a direct URL guess 404'd); M.G.L. Chapter 131, Sec. 40 (the Wetlands Protection Act, including the Rivers Protection Act's riverfront-area buffer amendment); 310 CMR 15.000 (Title 5, the private sewage/septic system regulation, with its real related-party transfer-inspection exemptions) and its enabling authority M.G.L. Chapter 21A, Sec. 13; M.G.L. Chapter 64G (short-term rental registration and tax); M.G.L. Chapter 183A (the Massachusetts Condominium Act). A small number of Massachusetts-specific facts (254 CMR advertising/escrow-account specifics, 105 CMR 410 State Sanitary Code minimums, the caveat-emptor property-disclosure doctrine, and the Land Court/Torrens registered-land system) could not be independently re-fetched live this session (mass.gov/sec.state.ma.us blocked with 403s, and WebSearch's session-wide budget was exhausted partway through this build) -- these are deliberately hedged in-bank to general framing rather than an invented pinpoint citation, consistent with this project's grounding standard, while still reflecting well-established, stable Massachusetts real estate practice facts rather than fabrications. Standard national real-estate/appraisal/finance/contract-law/math content not tied to a Massachusetts-specific statute is sourced to 'national real estate practice principles' framing throughout. Price set at $29.99 (2999 cents) to match this project's standardized Real Estate Broker track rate (nj_re_broker.json, tn_re_broker.json, va_re_broker.json, az_re_broker.json, ny_re_broker.json, ga_re_broker.json, pa_re_broker.json, ca_re_broker.json, fl_re_broker.json, oh_re_broker.json, tx_re_broker.json, mi_re_broker.json). This bank was drafted across six parallel content-authoring passes grouped by the real content-outline topic clusters, each pass instructed to draft every question with the correct answer as choice_a and to write to and self-verify an explicit absolute output path (following the standing lesson from this campaign's prior states about drafting agents mistakenly writing to a wrong nested path). No cross-bucket near-duplicates were found this time on a source_note-citation cross-check across all 20 files. Answers were deterministically rotated into final A/B/C/D position via scripts/tracks/rotate_ma_re_broker_answers.js (global sequential-cycle rotation across all 20 bucket files combined, in file order). All draft questions passed an automated schema/weight-range/distinct-choice validation pass, and were additionally run through this project's standard Jaccard-similarity dedup check (scripts/build-track-batch.js) at build time to remove any further exact or near-duplicate items before loading. 532 raw questions drafted against a 115-item exam -- a 4.63:1 pool ratio, comfortably clearing the standing 4:1 new-track floor without needing a backfill pass, unlike Virginia's build in this same campaign. POST-BUILD CORRECTION (2026-09-02): discovered this build's six drafting passes had been given a per-bucket target computed from a fixed item-count-times-multiplier formula, and 7 of the resulting buckets (Duties and Powers of the Board, Massachusetts Contract Forms, Licensing Requirements, Massachusetts Consumer Protection Laws, Massachusetts Environmental Issues and Hazardous Materials, Massachusetts Fair Housing Law, Property Management) landed suspiciously exactly on that target -- clear anchoring, not a genuine content ceiling. Standing policy corrected project-wide: pool ratios are a floor to check after drafting, never a target given to a drafting agent. Ran a full backfill: de-rotated all 20 files back to the choice_a-correct convention, relaunched the 7 flagged topics with no ceiling (added 19/9/20/10/11/21/24 respectively), re-checked cross-bucket dedup (0 new duplicates), re-rotated the full set, and rebuilt. FINAL: 646 questions (up from 532) -- a 5.62:1 pool ratio, fully reloaded into D1 (532 old rows deleted, 646 new rows inserted, verified by count).
